_comment: REAL GATT enumeration from the owner's WHOOP 5.0 MG strap, 2026-08-03.
This is the ADR-0012 acceptance-gate evidence. Recorded verbatim except for
the scrubs below (CLAUDE.md §6.2: scrub identifiers before committing).
SCRUBBED: the advertised device name carried a device serial ('WHOOP MG<serial>')
and the address is a host-local CoreBluetooth UUID. Neither is needed to read
the protocol shape, and both identify a specific physical device.
Why keep this at all: it is the baseline. WHOOP pushes firmware through the
official app (risk #9), and the ONLY way to notice the protocol moving under
us is to have written down what it looked like when it worked.
verdict: GATE PASSED — fd4b (5.0/MG) service family present, 5 characteristic(s)

0000180d-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.name: Heart Rate (SIG)
0000180d-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb.note: 2a37 is the standard Heart Rate Measurement characteristic. Live HR is therefore readable with NO proprietary protocol — a fallback path independent of the fd4b drain.

fd4b0001-cce1-4033-93ce-002d5875f58a.name: WHOOP 5.0/MG proprietary family
fd4b0001-cce1-4033-93ce-002d5875f58a.note: whoop-vault documents fd4b0002-0007 on firmware r52 'Maverick'. THIS MG EXPOSES FIVE, NOT SIX — fd4b0006 is absent. That is the MG-variant divergence ADR-0012 named as residual risk, now a concrete known difference.
